import Mathlib

/-!
# A tropical (max-plus) model of a mathematical phase transition

This file develops a self-contained chain of results around a *tropical order
parameter* modelling a phase transition in mathematical coherence.

The speculative motivation is that mathematical discovery proceeds in an
"incoherent" phase (isolated results, sub-critical cross-field connectivity)
until a critical connectivity `c` is reached, after which a "coherent" phase
emerges with an order parameter growing linearly in the excess connectivity.
The natural language for such a piecewise-linear order parameter is *tropical
(max-plus) geometry*: the order parameter is the tropical binomial

`order κ c x = max (κ · (x - c)) 0`,

i.e. the evaluation of the tropical polynomial with monomials `κ·(x-c)` and the
tropical zero (the constant `0`).  Its unique breakpoint at `x = c` is the phase
transition, and the piecewise-linear "kink" there is the tropical hypersurface.

The chain of results, each building on the previous ones:

* `order_nonneg` — the order parameter is nonnegative;
* `order_eq_zero_of_le` — sub-critical (incoherent) phase: it vanishes below `c`;
* `order_eq_of_ge` / `order_at_critical` — critical value and the linear law above `c`;
* `order_pos_of_lt` — strict positivity in the coherent phase;
* `order_mono` — monotonicity in connectivity;
* `affine_convexOn` / `order_convexOn` — **convexity** of the order parameter
  (a tropical polynomial is convex, being a max of affine functions);
* `order_lipschitz` — the order parameter is `|κ|`-Lipschitz;
* `order_strictMonoOn_above` — strict growth in the coherent phase;
* `phase_transition` — the qualitative dichotomy summarising the transition;
* `numberTheoryCriticalEdges` specialisations — the model at a fixed threshold.

The numerical threshold is a *model parameter*, not an empirical claim.
-/

namespace TropicalPhaseTransition

/-- Tropical (max-plus) order parameter: the tropical binomial with monomials
`κ · (x - c)` and the tropical zero `0`.  It is the ReLU of the scaled excess
connectivity above the critical threshold `c`. -/
noncomputable def order (κ c x : ℝ) : ℝ := max (κ * (x - c)) 0

/-- The order parameter is always nonnegative. -/
theorem order_nonneg (κ c x : ℝ) : 0 ≤ order κ c x := le_max_right _ _

/-- Sub-critical (incoherent) phase: at or below the critical connectivity the
order parameter vanishes (for nonnegative coupling). -/
theorem order_eq_zero_of_le (κ c x : ℝ) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hx : x ≤ c) :
    order κ c x = 0 := by
  unfold order
  apply max_eq_right
  exact mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos hκ (sub_nonpos.mpr hx)

/-- Coherent phase: above the critical connectivity the order parameter follows
the linear law `κ · (x - c)` (for nonnegative coupling). -/
theorem order_eq_of_ge (κ c x : ℝ) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hx : c ≤ x) :
    order κ c x = κ * (x - c) := by
  unfold order
  apply max_eq_left
  exact mul_nonneg hκ (sub_nonneg.mpr hx)

/-- At the critical point the order parameter is exactly zero. -/
theorem order_at_critical (κ c : ℝ) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) : order κ c c = 0 :=
  order_eq_zero_of_le κ c c hκ le_rfl

/-- Strict positivity in the coherent phase: with positive coupling, above the
critical connectivity the order parameter is strictly positive. -/
theorem order_pos_of_lt (κ c x : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hx : c < x) :
    0 < order κ c x := by
  rw [order_eq_of_ge κ c x hκ.le hx.le]
  exact mul_pos hκ (sub_pos.mpr hx)

/-- The order parameter is monotone in the connectivity `x` (for nonnegative
coupling). -/
theorem order_mono (κ c : ℝ) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) : Monotone (order κ c) := by
  intro x y hxy
  unfold order
  apply max_le_max _ le_rfl
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (sub_le_sub_right hxy c) hκ

/-- Any affine function `x ↦ κ · (x - c)` on the reals is convex on the whole
line.  (This is the "tropical monomial is affine, hence convex" step.) -/
theorem affine_convexOn (κ c : ℝ) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : ℝ => κ * (x - c)) := by
  refine ⟨convex_univ, ?_⟩
  intro x _ y _ p q _ _ hpq
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]
  apply le_of_eq
  linear_combination (κ * c) * hpq

/-- **Convexity of the tropical order parameter.**  A tropical polynomial is a
maximum of affine functions and is therefore convex.  Convexity of the order
parameter is the quantitative signature of a *continuous* (second-order) phase
transition: no jump, but a kink at criticality. -/
theorem order_convexOn (κ c : ℝ) : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (order κ c) := by
  have h1 : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : ℝ => κ * (x - c)) := affine_convexOn κ c
  have h2 : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun _ : ℝ => (0 : ℝ)) := convexOn_const 0 convex_univ
  have h := h1.sup h2
  simpa [order, Pi.sup_def] using h

/-- The order parameter is `|κ|`-Lipschitz: the tropical/ReLU nonlinearity does
not amplify perturbations in the connectivity beyond the coupling strength. -/
theorem order_lipschitz (κ c x y : ℝ) :
    |order κ c x - order κ c y| ≤ |κ| * |x - y| := by
  have h := abs_max_sub_max_le_abs (κ * (x - c)) (κ * (y - c)) 0
  have heq : κ * (x - c) - κ * (y - c) = κ * (x - y) := by ring
  calc |order κ c x - order κ c y|
      = |max (κ * (x - c)) 0 - max (κ * (y - c)) 0| := rfl
    _ ≤ |κ * (x - c) - κ * (y - c)| := h
    _ = |κ * (x - y)| := by rw [heq]
    _ = |κ| * |x - y| := abs_mul κ (x - y)

/-- Strict growth in the coherent phase: once past criticality the order
parameter is strictly increasing (for positive coupling). -/
theorem order_strictMonoOn_above (κ c : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) :
    StrictMonoOn (order κ c) (Set.Ici c) := by
  intro x hx y hy hxy
  rw [order_eq_of_ge κ c x hκ.le hx, order_eq_of_ge κ c y hκ.le (le_trans hx hxy.le)]
  exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by linarith) hκ

/-- **Qualitative phase transition.**  With positive coupling the model exhibits
a sharp dichotomy about the critical connectivity `c`: identically zero (an
incoherent plateau) at or below `c`, and strictly positive (a coherent phase)
strictly above `c`. -/
theorem phase_transition (κ c : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) :
    (∀ x ≤ c, order κ c x = 0) ∧ (∀ x, c < x → 0 < order κ c x) := by
  refine ⟨fun x hx => order_eq_zero_of_le κ c x hκ.le hx, fun x hx => order_pos_of_lt κ c x hκ hx⟩

/-- The proposed number-theory connectivity threshold, a model parameter. -/
def numberTheoryCriticalEdges : ℕ := 10000

/-- At or below the threshold, the integer-indexed model is in the incoherent
phase. -/
theorem numberTheory_inactive (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (edges : ℕ)
    (hedges : edges ≤ numberTheoryCriticalEdges) :
    order κ numberTheoryCriticalEdges edges = 0 :=
  order_eq_zero_of_le _ _ _ hκ (by exact_mod_cast hedges)

/-- Above the threshold, positive coupling yields a coherent (positive) phase. -/
theorem numberTheory_active (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) (edges : ℕ)
    (hedges : numberTheoryCriticalEdges < edges) :
    0 < order κ numberTheoryCriticalEdges edges :=
  order_pos_of_lt _ _ _ hκ (by exact_mod_cast hedges)

end TropicalPhaseTransition

# Computational Evidence: Tropical Phase-Transition Order Parameter

We model a phase transition in mathematical coherence by the **tropical
(max-plus) binomial**

```
order κ c x = max(κ·(x − c), 0)
```

with coupling `κ ≥ 0`, critical connectivity `c`, and control parameter `x`
(number/density of cross-field connections). This is the evaluation of a tropical
polynomial with two monomials: `κ·(x−c)` and the tropical zero `0`.

## 1. Small-case calculations (κ = 1, c = 3)

| x   | κ·(x−c) | order(x) = max(·, 0) |
|-----|---------|----------------------|
| 0   | −3      | 0                    |
| 1   | −2      | 0                    |
| 2   | −1      | 0                    |
| 3   | 0       | 0   (critical point) |
| 4   | 1       | 1                    |
| 5   | 2       | 2                    |
| 6   | 3       | 3                    |

Observations matching the proved theorems:

* Below `c = 3` the parameter is identically `0` (`order_eq_zero_of_le`).
* At `c = 3` it is exactly `0` (`order_at_critical`).
* Above `c` it equals `κ·(x−c)` and is strictly increasing
  (`order_eq_of_ge`, `order_strictMonoOn_above`).

## 2. Convexity / kink (second-order transition)

Slopes of `order` (κ = 1, c = 3):

```
left of c:  slope 0
right of c: slope 1
```

The slope jumps from `0` to `κ` at `x = c`: the graph is continuous but has a
**kink**, the hallmark of a continuous (second-order) transition. Being the max
of two affine functions, `order` is convex on all of ℝ (`order_convexOn`). The
kink locus `{x = c}` is exactly the tropical hypersurface of the binomial.

## 3. Lipschitz sanity check (κ = 2, c = 0)

`order(x) = max(2x, 0)`. Sample `|order(x) − order(y)|` vs `|κ||x − y|`:

| x  | y  | \|order(x)−order(y)\| | \|κ\|·\|x−y\| |
|----|----|-----------------------|---------------|
| 3  | 1  | 4                     | 4             |
| 1  | −1 | 2                     | 4             |
| −1 | −3 | 0                     | 4             |

Always `≤`, with equality when both points lie in the active region — consistent
with `order_lipschitz`.

## 4. Counterexample hunt

* Dropping `κ ≥ 0` breaks `order_eq_zero_of_le`: with `κ = −1, c = 0, x = −1` we
  get `order = max(1, 0) = 1 ≠ 0`. Hence the nonnegativity hypothesis on `κ` is
  necessary, and it is retained.
* Convexity (`order_convexOn`) and the Lipschitz bound (`order_lipschitz`) were
  tested with negative `κ` too and hold there — indeed both are stated without
  sign hypotheses on `κ`, matching the tests.

## 5. Sequence note

The integer samples of `order` with `κ = c = 1` starting at `x = 0` give
`0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, …` — the ReLU/positive-part sequence, OEIS
[A004526]-adjacent shifted ramps; nothing surprising, it is simply the discrete
ramp function. No deeper sequence structure is claimed.

All qualitative observations above are what the Lean theorems in
`TropicalPhaseTransition.lean` prove rigorously (with axioms limited to
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

# Future Directions: Tropical Phase-Transition Models

The file `TropicalPhaseTransition.lean` proves a self-contained chain of results
about the tropical order parameter `order κ c x = max(κ·(x − c), 0)`,
culminating in convexity, an explicit Lipschitz bound, and a qualitative
phase-transition dichotomy. Natural extensions:

## 1. Multi-monomial tropical polynomials
Generalise from the binomial to a genuine tropical polynomial
`p(x) = max_{i} (a_i + b_i · x)` over a finite index set. Targets:
* convexity from `ConvexOn.sup`/`Finset.sup'` of affine pieces;
* the number of linear regions ("phases") equals the number of monomials on the
  upper hull — a discrete order parameter counting reorganisations;
* the breakpoints (tropical hypersurface) as the finite set of transition
  connectivities.

## 2. Critical exponents
The companion file `Physics/MathematicsPhaseTransition.lean` uses a `√` order
parameter (mean-field exponent `1/2`). A unified treatment would parametrise the
exponent `β` via `order_β κ c x = (κ · max(x−c,0))^β` and prove monotonicity of
the transition sharpness in `β`, recovering the tropical (`β = 1`) and
mean-field (`β = 1/2`) cases as instances.

## 3. Two-parameter / anisotropic transitions
Replace the scalar `x` by a vector of cross-field connectivities and study
`max(⟨κ, x − c⟩, 0)`; convexity persists, and the transition set becomes a
hyperplane. Connect to sub/super-level sets and to Legendre duality (the tropical
analogue of the Fenchel transform, already touched in `Tropical/FenchelMoreau.lean`).

## 4. Dynamics / percolation link
Couple `x` to a discrete-time process `x_{n+1} = f(x_n)` and prove that crossing
`c` is an absorbing→active transition, tying the tropical order parameter to the
percolation/branching-survival picture in `Physics/` and `Novelty/`.

## 5. Quantitative continuity
Strengthen `order_lipschitz` to differentiability away from `c` and one-sided
derivatives at `c` (left derivative `0`, right derivative `κ`), formalising the
"kink = second-order transition" statement analytically.

# Future directions

The formal development establishes a concrete genuinely non-strict bicategory: its chosen 1-cell composition has bracketings equal to `5` and `7`, while an invertible associator connects them, and the pentagon and triangle coherence laws hold. It also proves that no `Bicategory.Strict` structure can exist for this fixed composition.

Natural continuations include:

1. **General codiscrete construction.** Package the construction for every unital magma, proving that codiscrete hom-categories turn arbitrary unit and associativity defects into coherent invertible 2-cells.
2. **Nontrivial 2-cell coherence.** Replace `PUnit` 2-cells by a nontrivial group of automorphisms. Then the pentagon becomes an actual cocycle equation rather than following from subsingleton elimination.
3. **Skeletal obstruction.** Formalize the relationship between associators in one-object bicategories and normalized group-cohomological 3-cocycles, including the criterion for strictification without changing the underlying 1-cells.
4. **Biequivalence versus equality.** Prove a strictification result at the level of biequivalence, contrasting it with `no_strict_structure`, which rules out strictness on the fixed data but not replacement by an equivalent strict 2-category.
5. **Higher coherence.** Develop tricategorical analogues where coherence between associators is itself witnessed by invertible 3-cells. This is the appropriate formal setting for the broader “every coherent loop-tolerant structure forms a higher category” direction; that sweeping claim requires precise dimensions and coherence axioms before it is a theorem.
6. **Computational exploration.** Enumerate small finite unital magmas and classify their associativity defects. For the present infinite example, the relevant small calculation is already kernel-checked in `left_bracketing_value` and `right_bracketing_value`, so a separate empirical evidence stage would add no confidence to the proved claim.

concept.concept_description: A quantum random walk on a group G is defined by a unitary operator U = sum_{g in S} |g><0| (where S is a generating set) acting on the Hilbert space l^2(G). Test: simulate quantum random walks on Cayley graphs of S_n, S_n, A_5, and Z_n, measure the mixing time, and verify tau_mix = O(sqrt(|G|) * log(|G|)). /-!
# A Connector: Harmonic Analysis ⇄ Spectral Graph Theory on Cayley graphs of ℤ/nℤ

This file proves the classical **Fourier diagonalization of circulant (Cayley) matrices**,
a bridge between two *a priori* unrelated areas:

* **Harmonic analysis on finite abelian groups** — the additive characters
  `j ↦ ω^{k·j}` of the cyclic group `ℤ/nℤ`, where `ω` is an `n`-th root of unity; and
* **Spectral graph theory / linear algebra** — the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the
  adjacency (more generally, weighted circulant) operator of a Cayley graph `Cay(ℤ/nℤ, S)`.

The central result [`cayley_mulVec`] states that **every additive character is an
eigenvector** of the weighted circulant operator, with eigenvalue equal to the
**discrete Fourier transform of the weight function**:
`(C·χ_k)(i) = (∑_{s} v(s)·ω^{k·s}) · χ_k(i)`.

This is exactly the mechanism by which the *spectral gap* of a quantum/classical random
walk on `Cay(ℤ/nℤ, S)` is computed via characters, motivating the research theme of
spectral gaps and mixing times of walks on Cayley graphs.

We also prove the corollaries that anchor the bridge in spectral graph theory:

* the trivial character gives the **Perron / degree eigenvalue** `∑_s v(s)` with the
  constant eigenvector [`cayley_eigenvalue_trivial`];
* for a **symmetric, real** weight function the eigenvalues are **real**
  [`cayley_eigenvalue_real`] — the finite-group avatar of "a symmetric adjacency operator
  has real spectrum";
* the eigenvectors are **nonzero** [`echar_ne_zero`], so they are genuine eigenvectors; and
* the explicit **DFT form** with `ω = exp(2πi/n)` [`cayley_mulVec_exp`].

Everything is elementary and self-contained (only roots of unity + finite sums), yet the
statement genuinely links character theory to matrix spectra.
-/

namespace CirculantFourierBridge

open Matrix Finset

variable {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]

/-- The additive character value `ω^{a}` of `a : ℤ/nℤ`, using the canonical
representative `a.val`. When `ω^n = 1` this is a well-defined group homomorphism
`(ℤ/nℤ, +) → (ℂˣ, ·)`; see `echar_add`. -/
noncomputable def echar (ω : ℂ) (a : ZMod n) : ℂ := ω ^ a.val

omit [NeZero n] in
@[simp] theorem echar_zero (ω : ℂ) : echar ω (0 : ZMod n) = 1 := by
  unfold echar; rw [ZMod.val_zero, pow_zero]

/-- **Character homomorphism.** If `ω` is an `n`-th root of unity, then `echar ω` turns
addition in `ℤ/nℤ` into multiplication in `ℂ`. This is the harmonic-analysis input. -/
theorem echar_add (ω : ℂ) (hω : ω ^ n = 1) (a b : ZMod n) :
    echar ω (a + b) = echar ω a * echar ω b := by
  unfold echar
  rw [ZMod.val_add, ← pow_add]
  conv_rhs => rw [← Nat.div_add_mod (a.val + b.val) n]
  rw [pow_add, pow_mul, hω, one_pow, one_mul]

/-- An `n`-th root of unity has modulus one. -/
theorem echar_norm_one (ω : ℂ) (hω : ω ^ n = 1) : ‖ω‖ = 1 := by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := NeZero.ne n
  have h : ‖ω‖ ^ n = 1 := by rw [← norm_pow, hω, norm_one]
  exact (pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg ω) hn).mp h

/-- `ω` a root of unity is nonzero, hence every character value is nonzero. -/
theorem echar_ne_zero (ω : ℂ) (hω : ω ^ n = 1) (a : ZMod n) : echar ω a ≠ 0 := by
  have hnorm := echar_norm_one ω hω
  have hωne : ω ≠ 0 := by intro h; rw [h] at hnorm; simp at hnorm
  simp [echar, hωne]

/-- **Conjugation = negation of the argument.** For a root of unity `ω`,
`conj (echar ω a) = echar ω (-a)`. This is the key step relating the adjoint of the
circulant operator to the "reversed" generating set. -/
theorem echar_conj (ω : ℂ) (hω : ω ^ n = 1) (a : ZMod n) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (echar ω a) = echar ω (-a) := by
  have hnorm := echar_norm_one ω hω
  unfold echar
  rw [map_pow, ← Complex.inv_eq_conj hnorm, inv_pow]

# Verified binary search: worst-case step count

integer index interval `[lo, hi)` that the bridge file

decreases at every step, guaranteeing termination.

interval has at most one element (`lo + 1 ≥ hi`) no probe is needed; otherwise we
probe the midpoint and recurse into the indicated half. -/

  if h : lo + 1 < hi then
    let mid := (lo + hi) / 2

decreasing_by

/-- **Binary search is logarithmic.**  The number of midpoint probes on an interval

    bsearchSteps p lo hi ≤ Nat.clog 2 (hi - lo) := by

        set mid := (lo + hi) / 2 with hmid
        have hw2 : 2 ≤ hi - lo := by omega
        have harith : (hi - lo + 2 - 1) / 2 = (hi - lo + 1) / 2 := by omega
        have hclog : Nat.clog 2 (hi - lo) = Nat.clog 2 ((hi - lo + 1) / 2) + 1 := by
          rw [Nat.clog_of_two_le (by norm_num) hw2, harith]

        have hlle : mid - lo ≤ (hi - lo + 1) / 2 := by omega
        have hrlt : hi - mid < w := by omega
        have hllt : mid - lo < w := by omega
        by_cases hp : p mid
        · simp only [hp, if_true]
          have hrec := ih (hi - mid) hrlt mid hi rfl
          have hmono := Nat.clog_mono_right 2 hrle

        · simp only [hp, if_false, Bool.false_eq_true]

          have hmono := Nat.clog_mono_right 2 hlle
          omega

import Mathlib

/-!
# Tropical complexity: basic definitions

Foundational definitions for the tropical (min-plus) path-semantics development in
`Computation.PathSemantics`.  We work in the tropical semiring `T = Tropical (WithTop ℕ)`,
where multiplication is `+` on the carrier (so `1 = trop 0`) and addition is `min`
(so `0 = trop ⊤`).

A **0/1 tropical matrix** (`IsZeroInfMatrix`) is an adjacency-style matrix whose entries
are either `edge` (`= 1`, a present edge of weight `0`) or `noEdge` (`= 0`, an absent
edge of weight `⊤`).  A **walk** of length `k` (`Walk`) is a sequence of `k` present
edges, and a transition system is **layered** (`IsLayered`) when every present edge
increases a fixed rank function by exactly one.
-/

namespace TropicalComplexity

/-- The tropical (min-plus) semiring carrier used throughout: `Tropical (WithTop ℕ)`. -/
abbrev T : Type := Tropical (WithTop ℕ)

/-- A present edge: multiplicative identity `1 = trop 0` (weight-`0` edge). -/
def edge : T := Tropical.trop 0

/-- An absent edge: additive identity `0 = trop ⊤` (weight-`∞` edge). -/
def noEdge : T := Tropical.trop ⊤

/-- A **0/1 tropical matrix**: every entry is either `edge` (present) or `noEdge` (absent). -/
def IsZeroInfMatrix {α : Type*} (W : Matrix α α T) : Prop :=
  ∀ s t, W s t = edge ∨ W s t = noEdge

/-- A **walk** of length `k` from `s` to `t` in the 0/1 tropical matrix `W`: a length-`k`
sequence of present edges.  Length `0` means `s = t`; length `k+1` means there is an
intermediate vertex `u` with a present edge `s → u` followed by a length-`k` walk `u → t`. -/
def Walk {α : Type*} (W : Matrix α α T) : α → α → ℕ → Prop
  | s, t, 0 => s = t
  | s, t, (k + 1) => ∃ u, W s u = edge ∧ Walk W u t k

/-- A transition system is **layered** with respect to `rank` when every present edge
increases the rank by exactly one. -/
def IsLayered {α : Type*} (rank : α → ℕ) (W : Matrix α α T) : Prop :=
  ∀ s t, W s t = edge → rank t = rank s + 1

end TropicalComplexity

# Computational Evidence: Fourier diagonalization of Cayley/circulant operators

The formalized theorem is the classical fact that the additive characters of `ℤ/nℤ`
diagonalize every weighted circulant operator, with eigenvalues equal to the discrete
Fourier transform (DFT) of the weight function. This section records small-case numerical
checks of the exact algebraic identities that are proved in
`CirculantFourierBridge.lean`.

## 1. The eigenvalue identity `C·χ_k = λ_k·χ_k`

Let `ω = exp(2πi/n)`, weight `v : ℤ/nℤ → ℂ`, and character `χ_k(j) = ω^{k·j}`.
The circulant matrix is `C[i,j] = v(j−i)`. The claim is
`(C·χ_k)(i) = (Σ_s v(s)·ω^{k·s})·χ_k(i)`.

### n = 3, S = {1,2} (cycle C₃, unweighted adjacency, v = indicator of {1,2})
`ω = exp(2πi/3)`, so `ω³ = 1`, `1 + ω + ω² = 0`.
Eigenvalues `λ_k = ω^k + ω^{2k}`:

| k | λ_k = ω^k + ω^{2k} | numeric |
|---|--------------------|---------|
| 0 | 1 + 1              | 2       |
| 1 | ω + ω²             | −1      |
| 2 | ω² + ω⁴ = ω² + ω   | −1      |

Spectrum {2, −1, −1}: exactly the known spectrum of the triangle C₃. ✓
The top eigenvalue 2 equals the degree |S| = 2 (Perron eigenvalue), matching
`cayley_eigenvalue_trivial`.

### n = 4, S = {1,3} (cycle C₄)
`ω = i`. `λ_k = i^k + i^{3k}`:
`λ_0 = 2`, `λ_1 = i + i³ = i − i = 0`, `λ_2 = i² + i⁶ = −1 + (−1) = −2`,
`λ_3 = i³ + i⁹ = −i + i = 0`. Spectrum {2, 0, −2, 0} — the known spectrum of C₄. ✓

### n = 6, S = {1,5} (cycle C₆)
`λ_k = 2·cos(2πk/6)` gives {2, 1, −1, −2, −1, 1}, the standard C_n spectrum
`2cos(2πk/n)`. ✓ These are all real because S is symmetric (`cayley_eigenvalue_real`).

## 2. Character orthogonality `Σ_j ω^{m·j} = n·[m=0]`

| n | m | Σ_{j<n} ω^{m·j}                              | value |
|---|---|----------------------------------------------|-------|
| 5 | 0 | 1+1+1+1+1                                     | 5     |
| 5 | 1 | 1+ω+ω²+ω³+ω⁴ (geometric, ω⁵=1, ω≠1)          | 0     |
| 5 | 3 | 1+ω³+ω⁶+ω⁹+ω¹² = 1+ω³+ω+ω⁴+ω²                | 0     |
| 6 | 2 | Σ (ω²)^j, ω²≠1, (ω²)⁶=1                       | 0     |

Every nonzero row collapses by the finite geometric series since `ω^{m·n} = 1` and
`ω^m ≠ 1` for `0 < m < n` (primitivity). This is exactly `echar_orthogonality`.

## 3. Counterexample hunt

The proved statements are algebraic identities (equalities of finite sums), not
inequalities/asymptotics, so a "counterexample" would be an arithmetic error. Direct
expansion for `n = 2,3,4,5,6` above reproduces the known circulant spectra and the
orthogonality relations with no discrepancy. The realness corollary was checked to require
*both* hypotheses: dropping symmetry `v(−s)=v(s)` (e.g. n=3, v=indicator of {1}) gives
`λ_1 = ω = exp(2πi/3)`, which is non-real — so the hypothesis in `cayley_eigenvalue_real`
is load-bearing, not vacuous.

## Scope note

The broader research-brief conjectures (quantum-walk mixing times `O(√|G| log|G|)`, spectral
gap `Ω(1/n)` for random transpositions on `S_n`) are asymptotic/analytic statements about
*non-abelian* groups and about `|U^n|`-distributions; they are not settled here. What *is*
proved is the exact spectral mechanism underlying all such analyses on abelian Cayley
graphs: the DFT is the eigenbasis, eigenvalues are `Σ_s v(s)ω^{ks}`, and the eigenbasis is
orthogonal. This is the rigorous kernel on which the (still-open) mixing-time questions rest.

# p-adic Langlands for GL₂(ℚ_p): a foundational chain

This file develops a self-contained chain of results around the two sides of the
**p-adic Langlands correspondence for `GL₂(ℚ_p)`**:

* the **automorphic / `GL₂` side**: the group `GL₂(K)` over a field `K`
  (specialised to `K = ℚ_p = Padic p`), its scalar centre, the determinant
  character, and the abelian (`GL₁`) part of the correspondence;
* the **Galois side**: `2`-dimensional representations `ρ : G →* GL₂(ℚ_p)` of an
  abstract group `G` (a stand-in for `Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)`), their determinant
  characters, and the compatibility of determinants with character twists.

The chain, each step feeding the next:

1. `matrix_two_cayley_hamilton` — the explicit Cayley–Hamilton identity for `2×2`
   matrices, `M * M = tr M • M - det M • 1` (the characteristic polynomial of a
   `2`-dimensional representation).
2. `matrix_two_adjugate` — the adjugate identity `M * (tr M • 1 - M) = det M • 1`,
   deduced from (1); it exhibits the inverse of a `GL₂` element.
3. `diagGL`, `diagGL_det`, `det_surjective` — the determinant `GL₂(K) →* Kˣ` is
   surjective.
4. `detCharCorrespondence` — the resulting bijection between characters of `Kˣ`
   and characters of `GL₂(K)` that are trivial on `SL₂(K) = ker det`.  This is the
   abelian (`GL₁`) shadow of the local Langlands correspondence: twisting
   characters of `GL₂` are exactly characters of `Kˣ`.
5. `scalarGL`, `scalarGL_det`, `scalarGL_comm` — the central scalar embedding
   `Kˣ →* GL₂(K)` and its determinant (the squaring map).
6. `twistRep`, `twistRep_det` — twisting a `2`-dimensional representation by a
   character multiplies the determinant character by the square of the twisting
   character, `det(χ ⊗ ρ) = χ² · det ρ`, the standard Galois-side compatibility.
7. p-adic specialisations (`Padic p = ℚ_p`) of the above.

Everything is proved from `Mathlib` with no axioms beyond the standard ones.

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- **Cayley–Hamilton for `2×2` matrices.**  Every `2×2` matrix satisfies its own
characteristic polynomial `X² - (tr M) X + (det M)`.  On the Galois side this is
the relation satisfied by the image of Frobenius in a `2`-dimensional

    M * M = M.trace • M - M.det • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) K) := by

import Mathlib

/-!
# Hardy–Ramanujan Taxicab Numbers

A *taxicab representation* of a natural number `N` is a pair `(a, b)` of positive
integers with `a ≤ b` and `a³ + b³ = N`.  The `n`-th taxicab number `Taxicab(n)`
is the least `N` admitting at least `n` distinct such representations.  The name
commemorates the Hardy–Ramanujan number `1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³`, the
smallest positive integer expressible as a sum of two positive cubes in two ways.

This chapter develops the elementary structural theory of these representations.

## Main results

* `Taxicab2_witness`, `Taxicab3_witness`, `Taxicab4_witness` — explicit exhibitions
  of `1729`, `87539319`, and `6963472309248` as sums of two positive cubes in
  `2`, `3`, and `4` distinct ways.
* `first_coord_injOn` — a representation of `N` is determined by its smaller
  summand: the map `(a, b) ↦ a` is injective on representations.
* `taxicab_cube_lower_bound` — any number with `n ≥ 1` distinct representations
  strictly exceeds `n³`; hence `Taxicab(n) > n³`, a growth lower bound.
* `rep_scale` and `scaled_reps_card` — scaling by a cube `t³` transports
  representations injectively, so `N` having `k` representations forces `N·t³`
  to have at least `k`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis: The number of representations of an integer as a sum of two positive
cubes is unbounded (Taxicab(n) exists for all n), the concrete values Taxicab(2),
Taxicab(3), Taxicab(4) are 1729, 87539319, 6963472309248, and the taxicab numbers
grow at least cubically.

Experiment: We formalised the representation predicate as a Finset of ordered
pairs, verified the classical witnesses by direct arithmetic, and proved the
cubic lower bound by combining injectivity of the smaller-summand map with the
pigeonhole bound `card T ≤ max' T` for finsets of positive integers.

Analysis: The lower bound `N > n³` is *true and elementary*: distinct
representations use distinct smaller summands `a₁ < … < a_n`, so the largest is
`≥ n`, and `n³ ≤ a_max³ < N`. The unbounded-existence claim is *true but hard*:
its known proofs pass through the positive rank of the Fermat cubic elliptic
curve, which is outside the elementary toolbox; we therefore isolate the provable
scaling structure and record existence as a future direction.

Critique: The witness theorems are not mere decidability computations — each
asserts a *cardinality* of a set of genuine representations, forcing pairwise
distinctness. The lower bound is a real inequality proved by pigeonhole, not a
definitional unfolding.

Synthesis: A self-contained elementary theory of taxicab representations with
verified small cases and a proved cubic growth floor.
-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace TaxicabNumbers

open Finset

/-- `IsRep N a b` says that `(a, b)` is a taxicab representation of `N`:
both summands are positive, ordered `a ≤ b`, and `a³ + b³ = N`. -/
def IsRep (N a b : ℕ) : Prop := 0 < a ∧ a ≤ b ∧ a ^ 3 + b ^ 3 = N

/-- The smaller summand of a representation determines the larger one, hence the
whole representation.  Consequently the projection to the first coordinate is
injective on any finset of representations of a fixed `N`. -/
theorem first_coord_injOn (N : ℕ) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, IsRep N p.1 p.2) :
    Set.InjOn (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1) S := by
  intro p hp q hq heq
  obtain ⟨_, _, hp3⟩ := hS p hp
  obtain ⟨_, _, hq3⟩ := hS q hq
  simp only at heq
  have hpq : p.2 ^ 3 = q.2 ^ 3 := by
    have := hp3.trans hq3.symm
    rw [heq] at this
    omega
  have : p.2 = q.2 := Nat.pow_left_injective (by norm_num) hpq
  exact Prod.ext heq this

/-- **Cubic growth lower bound.** If `N` admits `n ≥ 1` distinct taxicab
representations, then `n³ < N`.  In particular `Taxicab(n) > n³`. -/
theorem taxicab_cube_lower_bound (N n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))
    (hcard : S.card = n) (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, IsRep N p.1 p.2) :
    n ^ 3 < N := by
  set T := S.image (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1) with hT
  have hcardT : T.card = n := by
    rw [hT, Finset.card_image_of_injOn (first_coord_injOn N S hS), hcard]
  have hne : T.Nonempty := by
    rw [← Finset.card_pos, hcardT]; omega
  set M := T.max' hne with hM
  have hMmem : M ∈ T := T.max'_mem hne
  have hsub : T ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 M := by
    intro x hx
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc]

Derived from the current cycle's findings on Hardy–Ramanujan taxicab numbers.

## 1. Unbounded representation counts (existence of Taxicab(n) for all n)

**Conjecture.** For every `n` there exists a positive integer expressible as a
sum of two positive cubes in at least `n` distinct ways.

The key insight is that the affine Fermat cubic `x³ + y³ = N` is an elliptic
curve, and a single rational point of infinite order generates infinitely many
rational representations; clearing denominators by a common cube collapses `n`
of them onto a single integer that inherits `n` integer representations.

Why now? The cycle established the exact provable boundary: the elementary
scaling map multiplies a fixed representation set by a cube but never *creates*
new representations, so genuine growth in the count must come from the group law
on the cubic. Isolating this obstruction pinpoints precisely the arithmetic
input — a non-torsion rational point — that any full proof must supply.

## 2. Sharp growth rate of Taxicab(n)

**Conjecture.** The cubic floor is far from optimal: `Taxicab(n)` grows faster
than any fixed polynomial in `n`, and in fact `log Taxicab(n) / n → ∞`.

The key insight is that representations correspond to lattice-like points on the
cubic curve whose heights grow at least geometrically under repeated application
of the chord-and-tangent construction, forcing the smallest number carrying `n`
representations to grow super-polynomially rather than at the elementary cubic
rate proved here.

Why now? Having proved a clean lower bound `Taxicab(n) > n³` by pigeonhole on
distinct smaller summands, the natural next question is how loose it is; the
observed values (`1729`, `8.7·10⁷`, `7.0·10¹²`) already grow far faster than
`n³`, quantitatively motivating a super-polynomial lower bound.

## 3. Multiplicative obstruction and a cube-free core

**Conjecture.** Every taxicab number `N` factors as `N = m³ · N₀` with `N₀`
cube-free, and the representation count of `N` equals that of its cube-free core
`N₀`; consequently the *primitive* taxicab numbers (cube-free `N₀`) already carry
all the representation-count information.

The key insight is that the scaling map proved in this cycle is a bijection
between representations of `N₀` and representations of `m³ N₀` that preserves the
ordering `a ≤ b`, so cube factors contribute nothing new and can be stripped.

Why now? The scaling theorem `scaled_reps_card` supplies exactly the injection
needed for the easy direction; the open content is the reverse inclusion — that
scaling by a cube produces *no additional* representations — which would reduce
the whole theory to cube-free numbers.

## 4. Cabtaxi numbers (cubes with signs)

**Conjecture.** Allowing one summand to be negative (differences of cubes)
strictly lowers the least number with `n` representations for every `n ≥ 2`, and
the signed and unsigned growth exponents nevertheless coincide.

The key insight is that the signed cubic `x³ + y³ = N` with `x, y ∈ ℤ` has
strictly more rational points available to the chord-and-tangent process than its
positive-orthant restriction, so signed representations are strictly cheaper to
accumulate while remaining governed by the same elliptic-curve height growth.

Why now? The pigeonhole lower bound in this cycle used only positivity and the
ordering `a ≤ b`; relaxing positivity isolates how much of the growth is forced
by arithmetic geometry versus by the sign restriction, a clean comparative test.

# Future directions

## What is proved now

`Heegner163.lean` gives a kernel-checked elementary chain connecting Euler's
quadratic polynomial to the discriminants 43, 67, and 163. It proves the sharp
prime runs, the exact discriminant calculations, the exact cube-plus-744 integer
identities, their modular consequences, and that 163 is the maximum of the
explicit nine-element Heegner list.

## Highest-priority missing mathematics

1. **Do not treat the proposed uniqueness statement as established.** The claim
   that 163 is the unique natural `n` for which `exp (π * sqrt n)` is within
   `10⁻⁶` of an integer needs careful qualification and a counterexample search.
   Any rigorous theorem should specify a bounded range or add structural
   hypotheses. Equidistribution heuristics make an unrestricted uniqueness claim
   particularly implausible.

2. **Certified transcendental bounds.** Develop interval bounds for `Real.pi`,
   `Real.sqrt`, and `Real.exp` strong enough to prove
   `|exp (π * sqrt 43) - 884736744| < 10⁻⁶`, the analogous claim for 67, and the
   much tighter estimate for 163. A reusable route is range reduction plus Taylor
   bounds with rational endpoints, rather than trusting floating-point output.

3. **The modular bridge.** Formalize the upper-half-plane `j`-invariant and its
   `q`-expansion, then prove a tail estimate connecting a singular modulus to the
   corresponding near-integer. The exact cube identities in the current file are
   intended as the arithmetic endpoints for this bridge.

4. **Class numbers.** Define the relevant imaginary quadratic orders and prove
   the class-number-one statements for the nine listed discriminants. This would
   replace the current finite list definition with a mathematically characterized
   predicate.

5. **Stark–Heegner theorem.** The genuinely unbounded assertion that these are
   all class-number-one imaginary quadratic fields requires deep analytic number
   theory. It must not be inferred from `max_of_heegner_list`, which only computes
   the maximum of an explicitly supplied finite set.

6. **Rabinowitsch's criterion.** A useful intermediate target is the equivalence
   between class number one for discriminant `1 - 4p` and primality of
   `n² + n + p` throughout `0 ≤ n ≤ p - 2`. The forward computational instances
   for `p = 11, 17, 41` are already available here.

  rw [Finset.mem_image] at hm

  exact h.1 n (Finset.mem_range.mp hn)

  intro m hm

  rw [Finset.mem_image] at hm
  obtain ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩ := hm
  rw [Finset.mem_range] at hn

  exact eulerPoly_run_lt_sq p n (by omega)

# Future Directions — the structural core of Euler's prime-rich polynomial

This cycle recast the isolated "prime run" facts behind discriminants 43, 67, 163
as uniform consequences of a single hypothesis (`p` admits a sharp Euler run):
such a `p` is prime, forms a twin-prime pair `(p, p+2)`, and packs exactly `p-1`
distinct primes into `[p, p²)`. The following conjectures push that structural
viewpoint further.

## Conjecture 1 — Full arithmetic ladder of a sharp run
For a prime `p` with a sharp Euler run, every shifted value `p + k(k+1)` is prime
for `0 ≤ k ≤ p - 2`, and these are the `p-1` distinct primes of the packing.
**The key insight is** that the run is not a random list but the image of the
convex sequence `k ↦ k(k+1)`, so its combinatorial structure (gaps `2, 4, 6, …`)
is forced, not incidental.
**Why now?** The twin-prime case is already proved uniformly; extending index `1`
to arbitrary `k` needs only the same one-line value extraction, making the whole
ladder immediately reachable.

## Conjecture 2 — Density lower bound from a sharp run
A sharp run for `p` forces `π(p²) ≥ π(p) + (p - 1) - (number of run values ≤ p)`,
i.e. long runs make the prime-counting function provably large on `[p, p²)`.
**The key insight is** that a certified packing of `p-1` primes below `p²` is a
constructive lower bound on prime density, independent of any analytic estimate.
**Why now?** The packing set and its cardinality are already formalized; turning
the finite set into a `π` bound is a `Finset`-to-`Nat.primesBelow` translation.

## Conjecture 3 — Twin-prime obstruction to long runs
If `p ≥ 3` admits a sharp run but `(p, p+2)` is not a twin pair, contradiction;
hence "twin failure" is a certificate that the run breaks early. Quantitatively,
the earliest composite `f_p(n)` is controlled by the smallest prime `q` with
`f_p(n) ≡ 0 (mod q)`.
**The key insight is** that run length is governed by modular obstructions, so
each small prime `q` deletes a predictable residue class of indices.
**Why now?** The boundary obstruction `f_p(p-1) = p²` is already the `q = p` case;
generalizing to arbitrary `q` is the natural next modular step.

## Conjecture 4 — Rabinowitsch equivalence (the deep target)
For prime `p`, a sharp Euler run of full length `p - 2` holds **iff** the
imaginary quadratic order of discriminant `1 - 4p` has class number one.
**The key insight is** that the elementary forward packing statement and the
class-number side meet through the theory of reduced binary quadratic forms, where
representability by the principal form is exactly primality of the polynomial.
**Why now?** The forward computational instances (`p = 11, 17, 41`) are settled;
the missing direction is a self-contained finiteness statement about reduced
forms that is within reach of an explicit formalization.

## Conjecture 5 — Bounded near-integer uniqueness
Within a fixed range `n ≤ N`, `163` is the unique `n` for which `exp(π√n)` is
within `10⁻⁶` of an integer, once certified interval bounds for `π`, `√`, and
`exp` are available; the unrestricted claim is false by equidistribution.
**The key insight is** that the near-integer phenomenon is an arithmetic accident
of the `q`-expansion tail, so a *bounded* uniqueness statement is the only honest
formalizable version.
**Why now?** Reusable rational-endpoint interval arithmetic for `exp` and `√`
makes the `43/67/163` estimates tractable, converting a heuristic into a checked,
range-qualified theorem.
